page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-48-lssd is an Arm-based server instance powered by the Arm Neoverse-V2 architecture. It features 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs, operating with a single thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 384 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Additionally, the instance is equipped with 4020 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, while lacking integrated GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong multi-core capabilities and high memory throughput. The Neoverse-V2 processor achieves a multi-core stress-ng score of 86659.83, placing it in the top 25% of tested servers, while its single-core performance remains in the average tier. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 334.84 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 158.43 GB/sec for write operations. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression performance is exceptionally strong, reaching 532.16 GB/sec, which ranks in the top 10% of benchmarked instances.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the Arm64 architecture provides high resource density and power efficiency, offering a favorable performance-per-watt profile for memory-intensive workloads. However, the lack of hardware-assisted x86 vector extensions and hyper-threading represents a tradeoff for legacy software or specialized matrix math workloads. This instance is highly suited for memory-intensive databases, large-scale data processing, multi-threaded decompression tasks, and storage-heavy workloads requiring fast local NVMe access.
